title: Global Inventory Synchronization for OmniRetail
business: OmniRetail, a multinational clothing chain, needs to maintain a unified view of product stock across thousands of physical stores and regional warehouses to prevent overselling.
problem: Local databases at each store cannot communicate in real-time, leading to inconsistent stock levels where a customer might purchase an item online that was just sold out in a physical location.
solution: Implementing a distributed system that coordinates independent networked computers as one logical service allows OmniRetail to treat disparate regional databases as a single, consistent inventory pool through replication and consensus protocols.
steps: Identify the primary data partitions across regional data centers to enable sharding.
Implement a consensus-based replication protocol to ensure all nodes agree on the current stock count.
Deploy a message broker to handle asynchronous updates between the physical store POS systems and the central logical service.
Configure conflict resolution policies to handle concurrent updates to the same SKU from different geographic regions.
Monitor node health to ensure the logical service remains available even if individual regional nodes fail.
outcome: OmniRetail achieves a unified inventory state, significantly reducing overselling incidents and improving customer trust in online stock availability.
limitation: The primary trade-off is the latency introduced by consensus protocols; to check for this, engineers must monitor the time taken for a write operation to be acknowledged by a majority of nodes.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for OmniRetail, what is the primary reason for adopting a distributed system?
options: To eliminate the need for physical store databases entirely
To coordinate independent networked computers as one logical service
To increase the physical speed of the network cables
To reduce the total number of items sold in stores
questions.explanation: The scenario describes using a distributed system to unify disparate regional databases into a single service to solve inventory inconsistency.
questions.evidence: Implementing a distributed system that coordinates independent networked computers as one logical service allows OmniRetail to treat disparate regional databases as a single, consistent inventory pool through replication and consensus protocols.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for OmniRetail, what is the main limitation of the proposed solution?
options: The system cannot handle more than ten stores
The latency introduced by consensus protocols
The inability to use message brokers
The requirement to use only one database node
questions.explanation: Distributed systems often face trade-offs between consistency and latency, specifically when using consensus protocols to ensure all nodes agree.
questions.evidence: The primary trade-off is the latency introduced by consensus protocols; to check for this, engineers must monitor the time taken for a write operation to be acknowledged by a majority of nodes.
